A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoPE research project. Their main text, equations, figures, algorithms, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on four synthetic and two real-world tasks, including LPP and calibration measurements, component ablations, and distribution-shift experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds results for semi-balanced transport, additional comparators, prior misspecification, and biased calibration sets.

M1.justification: V1 fixes both marginals in balanced optimal transport. V2 introduces RoPE*, replacing the simulated-data marginal constraint with a KL penalty controlled by rho/tau, permitting simulations to be down-weighted under prior mismatch (Section 2.3 and Algorithm 1). The original NPE and calibration fine-tuning stages remain.

E1.justification: The six original tasks remain, but v2 substantially expands assumption-violation scenarios: prior-mismatched pendulum populations, newly collected light-tunnel data with betabinomial parameter distributions, and calibration/test distribution mismatch (Appendices C and L). The existing vertically flipped light-tunnel scenario is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated NPE-RS comparisons across the six tasks and extends NNPE from tasks A–B to tasks C–F (Figures 1–2). V1 cited the NPE-RS source but did not evaluate that comparator and explicitly excluded NNPE from C–F. Existing principal baselines remain.

E3.justification: The original LPP/ACAUC metrics, 2,000-example test sets, and core training settings largely remain. Added protocols include tau sweeps from 0.1 to 1, controlled prior-mixture weights, and error-versus-distance evaluation using normalized-color MAE. NPE-RS additionally uses the 2,000 test observations for its regularization.

E4.justification: V2 adds prior-mismatch and tau sensitivity experiments, biased-calibration robustness tests, error analysis by distance from the calibration distribution, and corresponding posterior examples (Figure 3 and Appendices C/L). V1's component ablations, entropy sensitivity, and image-flip robustness analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both main comparison captions report means and plus/minus one standard deviation over three random draws and additional randomness. The appendices retain the fixed real-data split descriptions. No changed repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for RoPE*, NPE-RS, expanded NNPE comparisons, and the new robustness scenarios. Figure 3 shows benefits from relaxing transport balance under prior mismatch. Appendix L reports increasing prediction error away from the calibration distribution despite near-zero marginal calibration scores for larger calibration sets. These are additional findings under new conditions.

T1.justification: V2 formalizes semi-balanced transport, adds a Gaussian-offset counterexample and posterior derivation distinguishing misspecification definitions (Appendix A.2), and develops coupling/prior-support reasoning (Appendix E). The original self-calibration proof is retained for balanced RoPE. The new counterexample's final bias expression is incorrect: its preceding posterior mean implies lambda*n/(n+1).

C1.justification: V1 explicitly conditions its contribution on a correctly specified prior. V2 broadens the contribution to addressing and investigating prior misspecification while retaining the central calibration-set/OT approach. The introduction also qualifies the benchmark novelty claim as real-world SBI benchmarks providing ground-truth parameter labels.

C2.justification: V2 replaces prior misspecification as merely a future-work limitation with an implemented mechanism and interpretation of tau. It adds substantive discussion of biased calibration sets, overlapping versus disjoint support, the assumed prior covering the true distribution, and ACAUC's inability to assess joint calibration (Section 6 and Appendices E/L).

D1.justification: Appendix H newly documents M1 MacBook Pro timings and posterior sampling/cache counts; Appendix I explains construction of the SBI reference. Most architecture and training details are retained. The light-tunnel dataset identifier changes from lt_camera_v0 to lt_camera_v1. Both versions still promise a future full-experiment code link.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial Related Work section positioning RoPE against simulation-to-reality transfer, domain adaptation, semi-supervised/few-shot learning, generalized Bayesian inference, and robust SBI. Numerous newly cited works support these distinctions, substantially expanding v1's limited positioning.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction and motivation, gives misspecification a dedicated background subsection, expands the OT-benefits discussion, introduces Related Work, and reorganizes the appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text and redraws the six-task comparison as Figures 1–2 with direct method labels. It adds robustness displays and relocates the workflow and posterior illustrations to appendices. Existing corner/calibration plots are retained and renumbered. New Figure 15 reverses the SBI/prior reference labels relative to the main comparison.

improvement.justification: V1 identifies prior misspecification as potentially severely damaging and leaves unbalanced transport as future work. V2 implements and tests that extension, broadens relevant comparator coverage, and investigates biased calibration data, substantially strengthening applicability and empirical support. The new Gaussian bias-formula error and Figure 15 labeling error are localized drawbacks that do not outweigh these gains.
